headline: The new HRRR run shows one isolated downpour near 0.40 in around 12 to 1 PM Sunday, but no other independent model supports it; expect a steady light-to-moderate soaking Sunday with street flooding unlikely, channel at base flow.

summary.text: HRRR wettest 3 hours jumped from 0.02 to 0.40 in, all in one hour (12 to 1 PM Sunday). Other models barely moved, so treat it as a possible shower cell, not a trend.
Wettest 3 hours: HRRR 0.40, GFS 0.40 (tracks HRRR hour for hour), RRFS 0.10, ECMWF 0.09, NBM 0.06 in. HRRR is the outlier; storm totals 0.28 to 0.55 in.
Rating card consensus about 0.10 in (middle of HRRR 0.40 x 1.25 = 0.50, RRFS 0.10, NBM 0.06): none. Water in the street would need the HRRR cell to verify and stall overhead.
Dry Saturday. Light rain from about 7 AM Sunday; possible HRRR downpour 12:15 to 1 PM; broader models peak 1 to 7 PM Sunday. A brief shower around midnight, then light rain Monday.
Sunday's 7.9 ft high at 3:33 PM is modeled near 9.4 ft (about 1.6 ft surge) and overlaps the afternoon rain. Channel at Alameda 0.12 ft, far below Monitoring 3.18 ft.
Clear leaves from street drain grates and yard drains Saturday. No need to move cars. If a heavy cell hits around noon Sunday, snap timestamped photos of the street.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: Upper-level ridging keeps Saturday dry and warm; NWS forecasts Redwood City near 71, a degree short of the date's record. A low tracking along the Northern California coast clips the Bay Area Sunday into Monday. NWS San Francisco (12:22 AM Saturday) raised rain totals from yesterday: 0.25 to 0.5 in for most of the Bay Area outside the North Bay and mountains, which it calls beneficial with only nuisance ponding on roads and in low spots. Gusts of 25 to 35 mph Sunday. NWS also mentions the potential for isolated thunderstorms outside the North Bay Sunday afternoon, with lower confidence than in the North Bay. Another system Tuesday into early Wednesday is expected to bring up to 0.25 in to most of the Bay Area; it is just beyond this 72-hour window.

sections.title: Model trends
sections.text:
From 1 AM Saturday to 1 AM Tuesday, wettest 3 hours / storm total (changes since 7:25 PM Friday):
• HRRR (11 PM run, ends 10 PM Sunday): 0.40 / 0.47 in, nearly all in 12 to 1 PM Sunday (up from 0.02 / 0.03 in). The 15-minute HRRR puts about 0.10 in in each quarter hour from 12:15 to 1 PM, with zeros before and after.
• GFS: 0.40 / 0.55 in, the same 0.40 in hour as HRRR, matching it nearly hour for hour through Sunday evening, so it is not independent support (up from 0.14 / 0.23 in).
• RRFS (4 PM run): 0.10 / 0.28 in, about 3 to 6 PM Sunday, plus a 0.06 in hour around midnight (up slightly from 0.08 / 0.14 in).
• ECMWF: 0.09 / 0.32 in, about 1 to 4 PM Sunday (down from 0.24 / 0.52 in).
• NBM: 0.06 / 0.30 in, light and steady, about 4 to 7 PM Sunday (up slightly from 0.04 / 0.20 in).

The HRRR spike is a single isolated hour with dry hours on both sides, and none of RRFS, ECMWF or NBM shows anything above 0.06 in in any hour. That pattern looks like a convective shower cell that HRRR happened to place over the street, which fits the NWS mention of isolated afternoon thunderstorms but is a low-confidence detail. It sits just under the 0.40 in one-hour Yellow trigger. HRRR has under-forecast big local bursts before, so a cell like this can't be ruled out, but where it lands is close to a coin toss at this range. The broader picture is a steadier, beneficial soaking of roughly a third to a half inch.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
NOAA's Bay model (run ends 7 PM Sunday) has Redwood City highs running 1.4 to 1.6 ft above predictions: Saturday 8.6 ft at 2:27 PM modeled near 10.0 ft, Sunday 7.2 ft at 4:49 AM modeled near 8.8 ft, and Sunday 7.9 ft at 3:33 PM modeled near 9.4 ft. That Sunday afternoon high overlaps the ECMWF and RRFS peaks, and the possible HRRR cell falls on the rising tide a couple of hours before it, which would slow channel drainage if heavy rain did hit. The NWS Coastal Flood Advisory for Bayshore locations runs until 5 PM Sunday; NWS lists moderate coastal flooding into the weekend as a key message. It affects the shoreline and tidal sloughs, not Athlone Terrace directly.

Channel at Alameda de las Pulgas: 0.12 ft at 1 AM, flat between 0.10 and 0.13 ft for the past day (Monitoring 3.18 ft). Upstream of Caltrain: no reading since 5:13 PM Friday, when it was 0.07 ft (Monitoring 2.8 ft) with no rain at its gauge in the previous 24 hours.

sections.title: Uncertainty
sections.text: The main question is whether Sunday brings any short, heavy convective cell to the mid-Peninsula. Only HRRR (and the GFS blend, which tracks it) shows one, so confidence is low. If the next HRRR runs keep a 0.3 in-plus hour near the street, or RRFS picks one up, the rating could move toward sidewalk or yard ponding for an hour, especially if it coincides with the surge-boosted afternoon tide. If the cell disappears, Sunday is a routine soaking.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• Saturday is the day to clear leaves from street drain grates and yard drains before Sunday's rain.
• No need to move cars out of the cul-de-sac for this one.
• Around noon to 2 PM Sunday, if a heavy downpour does hit, take timestamped photos of the street and the grates; don't walk or drive through moving water.
• Stay off the Bay shore and low shoreline paths around the midday high tides through Sunday.
• This page will update by midday Saturday, sooner if the burst strengthens or shows up in more models.
